sections.title: Introduction
sections.body: The US Fish & Wildlife Service (FWS, the Service) is in need of a Drupal development group to rebuild the Invasive Carp Regional Coordinating Committee site as a small-scale content management system in the latest version of Drupal (currently Drupal 9). Working alongside the Service, the contractor shall provide expertise to work through a design review of the current site and then develop a new version to facilitate a full migration off the old environment.

sections.title: Background
sections.body: A content management system, or CMS, is an application used to manage and publish web content. It allows multiple users to contribute, create, edit, and publish content without needing to have a web development skillset. It can also provide version management and authoring workflow to keep webpages consistent. Historically, management of the Invasive Carp website has suffered from complex content entry procedures and bottlenecks due to lack of resources/expertise in managing html. The rebuild of this site in a modernized content management system aims to achieve a straightforward content entry workflow that can be easily adopted and improve upon prior challenges of managing the site.

sections.title: Assumptions
sections.body: The Service assumes the following in regard to contractor approach: • While it is intended that the contractor approaches the site rebuild effort with an eye towards design improvements, it is not expected to be a full-fledged redesign effort - the most important requirements are focused on ease of managing the content on the site (in other words, the Service does not intend to spend an abundance of time on a completely new design) • There are two main parts to the CMS: (1) A content management interface allowing content creators to work with content directly by inputting content via templates and (2) a front-end display that takes the content entered into templates and renders it as a cohesive working website. Content entry forms should be configured with ease of use/simplicity as a priority

sections.title: Statement of Work
sections.body: The contractor will be tasked with rebuilding the Invasive Carp Regional Coordinating Committee (ICRCC) website as a content management system in the latest version of Drupal (currently Drupal 9). It is anticipated that the effort will start off with a design review of the legacy site, to determine if and where it may make sense to pursue any notable changes during the rebuild. The current organization and structure of the site is well liked by its heaviest users, but the group remains open to suggestions on how to improve the user experience and how to best build upon the foundation that exists. Once there is an agreed upon strategy for the site rebuild and any design adjustments coming into play, the contractor would move forward into development and further migration efforts. The site currently houses and will continue to house the following types of content/pages (not exclusively limited to): 1. Background Info/About Us 2. Plans and Report library (documents) 3. Newsroom/News archive 4. Outreach and Resource materials 5. Species Profiles (4 carp species) 6. FAQ It is anticipated that FWS and the partnership organization resources will manage an overwhelming majority of the written content development and migration for the site, while the contractor will be expected to facilitate migration of document and media assets where logical.

sections.title: Technical Approach (10 points)
sections.body: The Offeror shall provide a detailed realistic description of the proposed technical approach/methodology to be used and how it will address the project requirements, scope, challenges, purpose, and vision for the Electronic Handbooks (EHBs) program. The Offeror shall demonstrate that its processes are compliant with Capability Maturity Model Integration (CMMI) Level 3 or ISO 9000 on Quality Management and provide written proof of CMMI Level 3 Certification or ISO 9000 family/series Certification at the time of quote submission. The Offeror shall demonstrate that all work activities associated with the proposed approach can be accomplished in a comprehensive manner. The Offeror shall demonstrate innovation in the proposed technical approach. Innovation is defined as continual evolution (i.e., modification, enhancement, and/or replacement) of the enterprise EHBs processing system to infuse new technologies and approaches as they become available throughout the life of the contract. The proposed approach should be results-oriented and improve e testing efficiency and the predictability of resourcing and scheduling needs. Furthermore, the approach should include a balanced input and output that is user friendly, simplistic and trackable. The Offeror shall demonstrate their ability to identify and deal with program risk, both in proactive and reactive (emergency) situations. Anticipated risks should be made clear and mitigation strategies presented proactively.

sections.body: Please note that the hypothetical projects are for evaluation purposes only and may not be awarded by the Government when the BPA contract is awarded. The Offeror shall describe practical approaches that could be used to address the following hypothetical scenarios (limit answers to 10 pages per scenario.) For the purposes of proposal evaluation, the Offeror is not expected to develop a fully conceived proposal. Rather, the intent is to show how the Offeror would approach the hypothetical requirement and the related present or past (within the last 3 years) experience they have delivering similar projects. The Offeror should note when their approach results in artifacts or deliverables. The response should include the following sections: 1) Requirements; 2) Assumptions; 3) Proposed technical design, 4) Proposed number and type of staff; 5) Approximate cost to complete each scenario and 6) Proposed timeframe to implement the scenarios. Please highlight if you have provided services of similar scope and complexity for the Department of Health and Human Services. Offeror shall include a write up on current personnel that have experience delivering similar projects and why their experience is relevant to this hypothetical project delivery. These individuals should be employees or current Consultants of the Prime Offeror. The Offeror shall respond to each of the five hypothetical project area scenarios listed in this BPA solicitation. Each of these projects will be evaluated on a 10-point scale.

sections.title: Technical Approach for Hypothetical #1, Cloud Readiness and Enhancements - 10 points
sections.body: HRSA Test Harness is an Enterprise Test Automation Platform that standardizes automated testing processes and promotes collaboration across multiple vendors to support the HRSAs IT mission. The framework supports industry standard testing methodologies such as Data Driven Testing (DDT) and Behavior Driven Development (BDD). It provides an interface to users to define workflows to automate functional testing for an application. These workflows can then be executed against various environments as the software propagates from lower environments to higher ensuring the integrity and quality of the software product. The solution provides the capability for users to create test suites within the application UI with little or no coding. The configured test suites can then be executed either on demand or on a schedule in any given environment. All tests provide detailed reports that allows the user to identify potential defects with the product(s) being tested. The Test Automation Framework natively integrates with enterprise products like Jira for incident management, Jenkins for CI/CD, JMeter for performance testing, and RedGate for test data generation.  Current Challenges Current Test automation Test automation framework is designed to support and implement the automation tests for EHBs. Solution shall consider refactoring / Re-engineering the existing Test automation framework for cloud adoption and readiness. Proposed solution shall also consider  disaster recovery, loosely coupled architecture for APIs, Test Framework execution by bureaus in a containers, incremental modernization, maintaining backward compatibility until the system is fully modernized and migrated, system performance, scalability and cost savings in cloud space using the combination of Infrastructure as Service (IaaS), Platform as Service (PaaS) and Software as Service (SaaS). HRSA is also looking for a riskless migration path to modernize the system in specified duration without impacting business and performance of the current system. Please describe your strategy and approach for Cloud readiness and modernization. Specifically, the Offeror shall address the following requirements:  Review and provide the strategy for cloud adoption and readiness.  Propose the Cloud readiness architecture for all the core components of test harness. The modernization strategy should align with continuous delivery principles.  Enhance Test Harness platform to natively support cloud API testing and provision for third party tools integration  Create service containers for portability, management and test execution.  Ensure Data integrity and protection during transit and at rest.  Cloud adoption strategy should include o Configure auto scaling for performance and maximum throughput o Monitor, measure and Enhance security posture for cloud adoption  Interfaces and systems need to be covered while planning the cloud migration o Detect coordination problems in cloud environment – this is to ensure the applications are well configured with cloud environment

This Self-service framework is used for implementing new test suites with minimal/no code modifications by the testing engineering team. Framework was built in selenium actions to support wide range HTML controls within EHBs. Import/Export utility to migrate the test automation scripts between various test environments. Test Harness API interface is used for bulk executing smoke test scripts during EHBs module releases and system maintenance. Framework supports parallel execution by setting up workflows and form properties from within the application UI. Integration with third party libraries, COTS products and multi-factor authentication to support any type of endpoint in a secured way. Current Challenges In a constantly evolving technology and usability environment, enhancements are ongoing and require frequent user engagement, usability testing, and a feedback loop. This poses several challenges in capturing different user perspectives, different changes to maintain and modernize the system to meet changing requirements with advanced technology.
